# Introduction
Air quality is measured using physical and chemical monitoring instruments on the ground, low-cost optical and electrochemical sensors, and orbiting satellites, which feed data into the Air Quality Index (AQI). Definition by (NOAA's Official Website).

## Background Information
The following information contains data collected by graduate students.

### Packages

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
```
## Interactive Map 
```{r}
#| label: fig-cbl
#| fig-cap: "Location of UMCES Chesapeake Biological Laboratory."

leaflet() %>%
   addTiles() %>%  # Default OpenStreetMap base tiles
   addMarkers(
       lng = -76.4533, 
       lat = 38.3191, 
       popup = "UMCES - Chesapeake Biological Laboratory"
 ) |> 
  setView(-76.4533, 38.3191, zoom = 8)
```
See @fig-scatter for the results.
```{r}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Interactive daily ozone concentration vs. temperature in New York."

p <- ggplot(airquality, aes(x = Temp, y = Ozone, color = factor(Month))) +
 geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
 labs(
   x = "Temperature (°F)",
   y = "Ozone (ppb)",
   color = "Month"
   ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(tooltip = "all")

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-airquality
#| tbl-cap: "Stats Summary"
psych::describe(airquality) |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

Our sample size is `{r} nrow(airquality)`.

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
